questions.q: Why does tool selection get harder, not easier, as the number of available tools grows?
options: The Claude API technically forbids more than five tools per request
The model's context window shrinks automatically as more tools are added
Tool count has no measurable effect on selection accuracy
More tools, especially similar-sounding ones, increase ambiguity about which one actually matches the current sub-goal, and each one adds tokens to every request
questions.explain: A larger, less organized tool set is both less accurate (more ambiguity between similar tools) and more expensive (every definition costs tokens on every request in the loop).

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe consolidating near-duplicate tools (like create_pr/review_pr/merge_pr into one manage_pr tool) as a routing fix?
options: Because consolidation has nothing to do with how the model selects a tool
Because it removes near-duplicate tools from ever competing for the same intent in the first place
Because the Claude API requires exactly one tool per integration
Because consolidation always makes a tool's description shorter, nothing else
questions.explain: When three overlapping tools become one tool with an action parameter, there's no longer ambiguity about which of three similar tools to pick — the choice collapses to picking the right action value.

questions.q: What is Anthropic's own tool search tool designed to solve?
options: Searching the public web for new tools to install
Replacing the need for tool descriptions entirely
Translating tool names into other human languages
Letting Claude discover and load relevant tools on demand, for systems with hundreds or thousands of tools too large to send in full on every request
questions.explain: Rather than carrying an entire huge catalog in every request's tools array, tool search lets Claude pull in only what's relevant to the current task.

questions.q: What does 'explicit routing, by hand' mean in this lesson's example?
options: Manually typing out each tool_use block instead of letting the model generate one
A lightweight classification step that narrows a large tool catalog to a plausible subset before the main agent call sees the full tools array
Removing all tool descriptions so the model has to guess
Always calling every available tool in parallel regardless of relevance
questions.explain: This mirrors what tool search does at the platform level, but implemented in your own code: classify the sub-goal, narrow to a few plausible tools, then let the agent choose among just those.

questions.q: Besides accuracy, what cost does a large, poorly organized set of tool definitions impose on every single request in an agent loop?
options: It has no cost — tool definitions are free regardless of count
It forces the model to switch to a cheaper, less capable version automatically
It adds tokens to every request, since every tool definition in the tools array is included each time, increasing cost per step
It permanently disables the agent's ability to call any tool at all
questions.explain: Each tool definition (name, description, input_schema) counts toward the tokens in every request where it's included — a bloated tool set is a recurring cost on every loop iteration, not a one-time one.
